source.title: Transformers for molecular property prediction: domain adaptation efficiently improves performance
source.authors: Afnan Sultan; Max Rausch-Dupont; S. Khan; O. Kalinina; Dietrich Klakow; Andrea Volkamer

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supporting information are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies pre-training dataset size in molecular transformer models and reports downstream property-prediction outcomes. This is a related extension to data-scaling questions, but it does not measure language-model held-out cross-entropy or fit the claimed power laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports molecular property-prediction performance, not held-out language-model cross-entropy. It does not vary parameter count or compute, fit power laws, or evaluate loss-minimising parameter/token allocations. The data-size sweep and downstream metrics are recorded as related results under fits_no_version; figures provide the metric values, while the text reports several comparisons and significance results.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It trains one ~89M-parameter BERT-like SMILES encoder on four pre-training set sizes (0%, ~400K, ~800K, ~1.3M molecules). It then scores frozen CLS embeddings with a random-forest regressor on seven ADME regression tasks. Pre-training loss is never reported, no power law is fitted or extrapolated, and parameters and compute are never varied. The downstream measure belongs to a molecular encoder, not a language model's downstream tasks, and there are only four data points. So it cannot speak to V1–V4, to V5's power-law form, or to V6's predictable improvement in language models. The record's own version statuses (all not_tested) contradict its 'tests/T3' label. The plateau result is kept as a related finding under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find that MLM pre-training helps but plateaus beyond ~400K–800K molecules. MTR domain adaptation on ≤4K domain molecules gives significant gains across all seven datasets. Their 400K MLM+MTR model beats MolFormer and is comparable to MolBERT, while a random forest on physicochemical descriptors remains strongest overall.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains molecular SMILES transformers and evaluates downstream regression metrics; it does not measure the original studies' held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit their loss scaling laws, or test their compute-optimal allocation method.
record.method_sensitivity: Pre-training dataset size and evaluation split (Butina versus random) affect reported downstream outcomes; the paper reports higher R2 under random splitting.

fits_no_version.finding: For a ~89M-parameter MLM-pretrained SMILES encoder with frozen embeddings plus random forest, downstream ADME performance improved over random initialisation but plateaued at ~400K–800K molecules. The full ~1.3M set was matched (3 datasets) or significantly outperformed (4 datasets, p<0.01) by the 30% or 60% subsets under Butina splitting; random splitting showed a similar pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In molecular transformer encoders evaluated by frozen-embedding property prediction, downstream performance stops improving, or slightly degrades, with pre-training data beyond ~400K–800K molecules, rather than improving steadily with data scale.

record.problems: The study measures molecular-property regression rather than held-out language-model loss, so its results do not establish the claimed language-model scaling laws. Per-size metric values in the pre-training-size figures are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported pre-training dataset-size sweep outcomes for the seven ADME datasets were left out; the results are represented as aggregate rows for each metric and split.

untested.parts: No held-out pre-training loss reported; no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation.
No compute budgets or parameter/token allocation.
Single architecture (12 layers, 768-dim); shape not varied.
Molecular SMILES modality, but no loss curve or power-law form is examined.
Downstream regression for a molecular encoder across four data sizes. No language-model downstream tasks and no prediction from loss or scale fits.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation/tranche ('tests', T3) conflicts with its own all-not_tested version statuses; corrected to discusses/T6. The study is relevant only as a related observation: a downstream data-scale plateau in a non-text modality with a frozen-embedding evaluation. Its confounds are a fixed 20 epochs (so a larger dataset also means more compute), cluster-stratified subsets, and random-forest probing. It should not be read as evidence against loss-scaling laws.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No power laws are fitted on small runs or evaluated for extrapolation to larger runs.
No compute budgets or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations are evaluated.
The study does not compare architecture depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study uses molecular SMILES, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in that modality or in another training regime.
The study evaluates downstream molecular-property prediction across data sizes, not downstream language-model task performance or its predictability from pre-training loss.
The study does not compare scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or compute-optimal allocations. Its data-size performance plateau is not a test of the stated fitting-dependence claim.

relation.reason: The study experimentally varies pre-training data scale at a fixed architecture and measures downstream performance, directly bearing on V6.

tranche.reason: The controlled pre-training data-size sweep supplies results qualifying V6: downstream improvement plateaus around 400K–800K molecules, and the full dataset sometimes performs significantly worse. V6 does not require held-out language-model loss or a fitted power law.

source_check.notes: No statements or verdicts are listed. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate; V6 warrants limits_scope for the Butina and random split conditions, while the study does not establish a predictive scaling function or test V1–V5 or V7.
